title: Hepatic and Renal Impairment PK Studies: FDA and EMA Design Expectations and Label Dosing Outcomes
summary: FDA and EMA expectations for hepatic and renal impairment PK study design, and the dosing recommendations they have produced in recent US drug labels.
body_markdown:
## Hepatic and renal impairment PK studies: FDA and EMA design expectations and recent label dosing outcomes


### Key takeaways


- **The renal guidance is current on both sides of the Atlantic.** FDA finalized *Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function: Study Design, Data Analysis, and Impact on Dosing* on March 15, 2024[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=172) . EMA's *Guideline on the evaluation of the pharmacokinetics of medicinal products in patients with decreased renal function* (EMA/CHMP/83874/2014) was adopted by CHMP on 17 December 2015 and took effect on 1 July 2016[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=23) .
- **Hepatic guidance is in flux at FDA.** FDA issued a draft revision, *Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Hepatic Function: Study Design, Data Analysis, and Impact on Dosage* , on September 2, 2026[244](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=244) . The May 2003 guidance it replaces, *Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Hepatic Function: Study Design, Data Analysis, and Impact on Dosing and Labeling* , has been withdrawn[253](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=253) . EMA's hepatic guideline (CPMP/EWP/2339/02) dates from August 2005[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=92)[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=93) .
- **Both agencies use the same basic logic.** A dedicated study is usually triggered when the relevant organ eliminates a meaningful share of the drug, or when impairment is otherwise likely to change exposure enough to affect dosing. Reduced "worst-case" designs are acceptable for screening. Dosing advice should come from exposure-response, not from the size of the PK change alone.
- **Recent US labels show the full range of outcomes.** Examples include stepwise eGFR-based regimens for renally cleared anti-infectives (UTEBZI, ZAYNICH)[155](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=155)[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=156)[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=157)[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=161)[162](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=162)[163](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=163)[164](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=164) , a fixed lower dose in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment (INLURIYO)[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=227) , a tapered moderate-hepatic regimen (JOURNAVX)[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=230) , and "not recommended" or contraindicated statements where exposure increases are large (COBENFY)[383](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=383)[416](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=416) .


### Governing documents


Topic FDA EMA


Renal impairment Final guidance, March 15, 2024[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=172) Guideline EMA/CHMP/83874/2014, adopted 17 December 2015, effective 1 July 2016[23](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=23)


Hepatic impairment Draft guidance, September 2, 2026 (not for implementation)[244](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=244)[252](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=252) Guideline CPMP/EWP/2339/02, August 2005[92](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=92)[93](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=93)


### Renal impairment studies


#### When a dedicated study is expected


**FDA.** A dedicated study is recommended when renal impairment is likely to alter the PK of the drug or its active metabolites because they are substantially renally eliminated. FDA defines "substantially" as at least 30% of the systemically available drug or active metabolite excreted unchanged in urine[355](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=355) . A full PK design is recommended for this category[178](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=178) . For drugs cleared mainly by non-renal routes, an effect of severe renal impairment cannot always be excluded, so a reduced study should be considered[356](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=356) . Therapeutic proteins above 69 kDa are listed among products for which a dedicated study may not be warranted[357](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=357) .


**EMA.** A study should be conducted for primarily renally eliminated drugs unless otherwise justified. A study is also recommended for primarily hepatically eliminated drugs, because renal impairment can change exposure through non-renal mechanisms[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=41) . The guideline gives examples of justified exceptions, each requiring justification. These include single or occasional administration without safety concerns, large proteins not expected to be filtered, no relevant systemic absorption, and drugs not indicated in renal impairment[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=29) . EMA also asks sponsors to consider studying renal impairment before the pivotal trial when specific treatment recommendations are likely, so that these patients can be included and appropriately dosed[43](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=43)[44](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=44) .


#### Study design


Element FDA (2024) EMA (2016)


Full design Renal function from normal through severe impairment or kidney failure not on dialysis[180](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=180) Full range, including ESRD where feasible. About 6 to 8 subjects per group is usually sufficient, but coverage across GFR matters more than equal group sizes. Include subjects at 20 mL/min or below[46](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=46)


Reduced design Severe impairment or kidney failure not on dialysis versus normal function. If no PK difference, no further study. If a clinically relevant effect, characterize the other levels[183](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=183)[184](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=184) Worst-case group, preferably GFR 20 mL/min or below without dialysis, versus controls[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=47)[48](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=48) . Staged expansion if effects at other levels cannot be excluded[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=47)[49](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=49)


Sample size Justified for precise estimation. Example: 95% CI within 60% to 140% of the geometric mean with at least 80% power[182](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=182) Prospectively define clinical relevance and justify the decision criteria, confidence intervals and significance level for reduced studies[50](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=50)


Population and controls Stable renal function, groups similar on PK-relevant factors, exclude interacting comedications[181](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=181) Chronic or stable renal disease, groups comparable on age, sex, weight and pharmacogenetics[51](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=51) . Control group reflects the renal function typical of the pivotal trial population, not necessarily normal function[52](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=52)


#### Measuring and classifying renal function


FDA recommends eGFR over estimated creatinine clearance because of its availability and clinical use, while still accepting measured GFR, measured CLcr or a contemporary validated equation[185](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=185) . Adult dosing recommendations should use absolute eGFR in mL/min (indexed eGFR multiplied by BSA/1.73), not mL/min/1.73 m²[186](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=186) . When Cockcroft-Gault is used in overweight or obese individuals, ideal or adjusted body weight is likely to be more accurate than actual weight[187](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=187) . One estimation method should be used across groups and pooled studies[188](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=188)[189](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=189) .


EMA prefers measured GFR using an exogenous marker where possible, particularly when a narrow therapeutic index makes a dosing cut-off critical[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=53) . It notes that creatinine clearance may overestimate GFR because creatinine is also secreted[54](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=54) . Dosing should also be based on absolute renal function in mL/min[55](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=55) .


Category FDA Table 1 (dedicated studies only) EMA Table 1


Normal or control ≥90 mL/min[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=191) ≥90 mL/min[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=56)


Mild 60 to <90[192](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=192) 60 to <90[57](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=57)


Moderate 30 to <60[193](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=193) 30 to <60[58](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=58)


Severe <30, including kidney failure not on dialysis[194](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=194) <30, not requiring dialysis[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=59)


ESRD Included in the <30 category if not on dialysis[194](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=194) <15, requiring dialysis[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=60)


FDA states these categories are strictly for dedicated renal impairment studies, not for classifying kidney disease[195](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=195) .


#### Dialysis and renal replacement therapy


FDA expects intermittent hemodialysis studies to include on- and off-dialysis periods, with dialysis typically started just before the anticipated Tmax[197](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=197) . They should use high-flux dialysis, and blood flow, dialysate flow, ultrafiltration and dialyzer model should be recorded[198](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=198) . Dialysis clearance is calculated as the amount recovered in dialysate divided by AUC over the session[205](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=205) . For drugs likely to be used in critically ill patients, FDA recommends evaluating CRRT separately because hemodialysis findings may not extrapolate[199](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=199) .


EMA similarly calls for dosing before and after dialysis. It warns that extrapolation between modalities can be misleading[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=63)[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=64) . A dialysis study is unnecessary when high protein binding, a large volume of distribution or high non-renal clearance make removal unlikely[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=65) .


#### Population PK as a supplement or alternative


Both agencies accept population PK from phase 2/3 trials when renal function is well represented. FDA states such analyses may suffice for the population represented, but a reduced study may still be needed if severe impairment is under-represented[179](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=179) . FDA lists the design elements needed: participants across a wide renal function range, accurate dosing and sampling times, unbound concentrations when appropriate, and active metabolite measurements[201](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=201) . EMA is more cautious. It notes that severe impairment and ESRD are commonly under-represented in phase 2/3 data and recommends a phase 1 full or reduced study when renal evaluation is indicated[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=67) . EMA also states that population models must not be extrapolated outside the studied renal function range[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=69) .


#### From PK data to dosing recommendations


FDA bases dosing on the relationship among renal function, exposure and exposure-response. A PK change does not necessarily require a different dose, especially for drugs with a wide therapeutic range[401](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=401) . Where adjustment is needed, FDA recommends exposure-matching to a reference group with acceptable benefit-risk, which need not have normal renal function[401](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=401) . Supporting approaches include simulations targeting the 5th to 95th percentile of reference exposure, or predefined no-effect boundaries[402](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=402) . Modeling should identify the renal function level at which dosing changes, rather than defaulting to study categories[403](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=403) .


EMA takes the same view: dose-adjustment cut-offs need not match the 30, 60 and 90 mL/min recruitment boundaries[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=73) . It asks for steady-state simulations showing target attainment just above and below each cut-off[74](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=74) . For active metabolites, recommendations should reflect the total active moiety, accounting for potency and unbound exposure[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=73) .


#### Labeling and SmPC expectations


FDA's Prescribing Information should summarize PK and PD (including in dialysis), renal elimination of the drug and active metabolites, clinical effects of the PK changes, and risk-mitigation measures such as dose or monitoring changes[405](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=405)[406](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=406)[407](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=407)[408](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=408)[409](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=409) . EMA asks for specific dosing advice in SmPC section 4.2, including an explicit statement when no adjustment is needed. If creatinine clearance rather than GFR was used in the PK study, the SmPC should say so[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=75) . EMA states that lack of data alone should generally not lead to a contraindication without a specific safety concern[76](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=76) .


### Hepatic impairment studies


#### When a dedicated study is expected


FDA's 2026 draft recommends a dedicated hepatic impairment study if any of these apply[319](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=319) :


- Hepatic metabolism and/or excretion accounts for more than 30% of elimination of the absorbed parent drug or active metabolites[320](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=320) .
- Small concentration changes could be clinically significant[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=321) .
- Elimination pathways are not adequately characterized[322](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=322) .
- The drug treats liver disease[323](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=323) .
- The drug is likely to be used in patients with hepatic impairment[324](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=324) .


A study may not be warranted for these products: drugs with less than 30% hepatic elimination and no narrow-margin concerns[326](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=326) , drugs entirely renally excreted[327](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=327) , single-administration products[328](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=328) , locally acting products with limited systemic exposure[329](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=329) , and volatile drugs eliminated through the lungs[330](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=330) .


EMA recommends a study when all three of these conditions hold: the drug is likely to be used in hepatic impairment, impairment is likely to significantly alter PK, and dose adjustment may be needed given the PK/PD relationship[94](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=94) . If no study is performed, the sponsor must justify the omission. Missing data may lead to restrictions, including contraindications[95](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=95) .


#### Study design


Element FDA draft (2026) EMA (2005)


Groups Mild, moderate and severe impairment plus controls. Studying severe impairment first may be reasonable, with the other groups added if a significant effect is seen[295](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=295)[296](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=296) Moderate impairment versus healthy controls is an acceptable screening design. If a significant effect is found, study milder and, if possible, more severe impairment[97](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=97)[98](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=98)


Controls Similar in age, sex, race or ethnicity, weight and relevant polymorphic enzyme or transporter phenotypes[268](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=268) Within-study normal-function controls matched on PK determinants. Historical controls are discouraged[104](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=104)


Subjects Record liver disease etiology. Exclude acute or acute-on-chronic disease. Laboratory values and clinical status should be stable before dosing[297](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=297)[298](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=298) Volunteers with hepatic disease are acceptable when studying patients with the intended indication is impractical[97](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=97)


Dosing Single dose if PK is dose-proportional and time-independent. Otherwise multiple doses, preferably to steady state. A lower dose may be appropriate if higher concentrations would be dose-limiting[303](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=303)[304](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=304) Single dose for linear, time-independent PK. Multiple dosing for nonlinear or time-dependent PK. Consider a lower dose for drugs with high first-pass metabolism[99](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=99)[100](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=100)


Sample size Example target: 95% CI within 60% to 140% of the geometric mean with at least 80% power[301](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=301)[302](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=302) Sized to detect a prespecified, justified clinically relevant difference[98](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=98)


#### Classification of hepatic impairment


Both agencies use Child-Pugh: class A (score 5 to 6, mild), class B (7 to 9, moderate) and class C (10 to 15, severe)[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=254)[101](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=101) . FDA asks for both total and component scores, including how ascites and encephalopathy were assessed (for example, with or without diuretics)[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=256) . FDA's draft allows NCI criteria in oncology but recommends Child-Pugh for hepatobiliary cancers and does not recommend NCI criteria in non-cancer patients[299](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=299)[300](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=300) . EMA notes that Child-Pugh was not developed to predict drug elimination capacity and that even normal hepatic function scores 5[101](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=101)[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=102) .


#### Unbound concentrations


FDA's draft is more prescriptive than EMA on protein binding. For high-extraction drugs (extraction ratio >0.7) with extensive binding (fraction unbound <10%), the unbound fraction should be determined at trough and peak[306](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=306) . FDA encourages the same approach for low-extraction (<0.3), highly bound drugs[307](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=307) . Any decision not to measure unbound concentrations should be explained, and samples should be archived for drugs that are not extensively bound[308](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=308) . EMA asks that unbound parent and active metabolite concentrations be analysed for highly protein-bound drugs[105](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=105) .


#### Analysis, dose development and labeling


FDA asks for impaired-to-control geometric mean ratios with 90% confidence intervals for total and unbound AUC and Cmax[261](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=261) . It also asks for exploration of PK relationships with individual Child-Pugh components[262](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=262) . The dose-development framework mirrors the renal guidance. The usual dose may be retained if exposure changes are not clinically significant. Otherwise, exposure-matching to a reference group should be used, supported by 5th to 95th percentile simulations or no-effect boundaries[474](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=474)[475](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=475)[476](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=476)[477](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=477)[478](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=478) . Population PK may suffice if hepatic impairment is adequately represented in trials, with a dedicated study filling gaps[456](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=456)[457](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=457) . Labeling should cover PK/PD in hepatic impairment, hepatic elimination, clinical effects and risk-mitigation measures[468](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=468)[469](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=469)[470](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=470)[471](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=471)[472](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=472) .


EMA asks for prespecified, justified PK changes that warrant dose adjustment[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=108) . Simulations may help identify doses and intervals meeting targets[109](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=109) . In SmPC section 4.2, sponsors should describe the studied subjects and not extrapolate beyond them, stating explicitly when no adjustment is needed[110](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=110) . Section 5.2 should describe the hepatic disease studied and state if hepatic impairment was not evaluated. A claim of no clinically relevant effect requires good justification[112](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=112) .

#### Patterns in the recent labels


- **Fold-changes alone do not set the dose.** BLUJEPA's 1.7-fold AUC increase in severe hepatic impairment led to "avoid use" because of QTc risk[368](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=368) . JOURNAVX's 1.5-fold increase in moderate impairment led to a tapered regimen rather than a simple dose cut[390](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=390)[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=230) . Both outcomes illustrate the exposure-response approach both agencies' guidance recommends[401](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=401)[108](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=108) .
- **Renally cleared anti-infectives get stepwise eGFR tables.** The UTEBZI and ZAYNICH dose steps track the graded AUC increases by renal function band[431](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=431)[432](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=432)[433](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=433)[155](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=155)[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=156)[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=157)[315](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=315)[316](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=316)[163](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=163) . ZAYNICH extends the table to eGFR 8 to 14 mL/min with or without hemodialysis[164](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=164) .
- **Large measured exposure increases, or absent data, can lead to restriction rather than dose adjustment.** COBENFY's at least 7-fold xanomeline increase in moderate hepatic impairment led to a contraindication[377](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=377)[383](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=383) . NEREUS, with no hepatic data at all, is labeled "avoid use" across all Child-Pugh classes[235](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=235) .
- **Labels flag where data stop.** UTEBZI states that data are insufficient for hemodialysis[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=159) . DATROWAY states that the effect of severe renal impairment is unknown[168](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=168) . This matches FDA's expectation that labeling convey what was and was not characterized[405](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=405) , and EMA's instruction not to extrapolate beyond the studied population[110](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/hepatic-and-renal-impairment-pk-studies-fda?showSourceNumber=110) .
